questions.q: Which taboo does Alan Watts set out to explore?
a: Who we truly are
How societies pick their leaders
Why religions disagree about God
What happens to the body at death
questions.why: The overview quotes the subtitle, on the taboo against knowing who you are.

questions.q: What false belief does Watts say most people hold about themselves?
a: That they are separate from the rest of the world
That they are powerless to change anything
That they are more capable than other people
That they are defined by the work they do
questions.why: Lesson 1 challenges the feeling of being a separate center of action facing an alien world.

questions.q: Why does Watts compare cause and effect to watching a cat through a hole in a fence?
a: We mistake parts of one whole for separate events
We only notice what we are already looking for
We trust our senses more than our reason
We assume that animals think like people
questions.why: Lesson 2 shows how a head, body and tail seen in sequence look like cause and effect.

questions.q: What does the German word Hintergedanken refer to in the summary?
a: Assumptions so deep we never question them
Thoughts we deliberately keep hidden
Memories that shape our childhood
Ideas we borrow from other cultures
questions.why: Lesson 2 translates it as thoughts behind the thoughts, the beliefs we take for granted.

questions.q: How does Watts suggest we view death?
a: As an opportunity and a gateway to growth
As a punishment for past actions
As an end that makes life meaningless
As something to ignore until it arrives
questions.why: Lesson 3 says other traditions treat death as a passage, and that remembering it can deepen purpose.
